response.consequence: Reminders marked `cancelled` for cancelled or rescheduled bookings, or edited workflows, are never cancelled at SendGrid. The attendee still receives the emails for those bookings. The `cancelled` rows stay in the DB and the cron retries and fails on every run.
response.explanation: The new cancel loop in scheduleEmailReminders.ts calls `client.request` from `@sendgrid/client`. The file only calls `sgMail.setApiKey`, which configures the mail service's own client. It never calls `client.setApiKey`. In the code I could see, the only `client.setApiKey` is inside emailReminderManager.ts (line 26), which this cron file doesn't import. The first `client.request` for a cancelled reminder therefore fails with an auth error. The surrounding try/catch swallows the error and only logs it. This also aborts the whole loop, so no later reminder is processed. No cancelled reminder is deleted from the DB or cancelled at SendGrid.
response.title: Cron cancel loop uses SendGrid client without an API key

response.consequence: Cancelled or rescheduled bookings can still send workflow reminders, or leave orphaned reminder rows, when the process stops before the unawaited promises finish. Failures are silent.
response.explanation: The old handler awaited the workflowReminder deleteMany calls inside Promise.all. The new code calls the async deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder without await or collecting their promises (handleCancelBooking.ts 485-491). The handler therefore returns after sendCancelledEmails without waiting for the Twilio cancel or the DB delete/update. Errors are swallowed inside those helpers with console.log. In a serverless runtime the response can end before the work finishes, which leaves SMS reminders scheduled at Twilio or reminder rows not updated, so a cancelled booking can still send reminders. The same pattern is in handleNewBooking.ts 964-976 for reschedules. The try/catch there cannot catch rejections from unawaited async calls, so it is ineffective. For reschedules, the email path with immediateDelete=true only cancels at SendGrid. It neither deletes nor marks the DB row, so the stale reminder row stays.
response.title: Reminder cancellation is fire-and-forget and no longer part of the awaited cancel flow

response.explanation: The new calls pass (reminder.id, reminder.referenceId), which matches deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?) and deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminderId, referenceId). Both helpers now delete or mark cancelled the workflowReminder row themselves, so the removed deleteMany calls are covered. Both helpers also catch their own errors.

Only emailReminderManager sets cancelled: true, so the missing method filter on the cancel query has no practical effect.

response.consequence: One bad reminder blocks cancellation cleanup for all the others. Cancelled rows pile up and get re-sent to SendGrid on every run. The only trace is a console.log.
response.explanation: The loop awaits client.request for each reminder inside a single try. The Prisma delete calls are lazy and only run when awaited, and they are only awaited in Promise.all after the loop. If any request throws, for example on a SendGrid error, a rate limit or a null referenceId, control jumps to the catch. The remaining reminders are never cancelled. The deletes already queued for earlier reminders never execute either, even though their SendGrid sends were cancelled. Those rows stay cancelled:true and are retried on every cron run.

other_findings.consequence: If the 401 is real, the first cancel request throws. The catch swallows the error and no cancelled reminder is ever deleted or cancelled at SendGrid, so cancelled bookings still get their emails sent.
other_findings.explanation: The file only calls sgMail.setApiKey (line 19). The default export of @sendgrid/client is a separate instance that never receives the key, and client.setApiKey is not called anywhere in the file. The new client.request to /v3/user/scheduled_sends is therefore sent without an Authorization header, so SendGrid should reject it with a 401. This is inferred from how the two SendGrid packages hold their keys. I did not run it.
other_findings.title: @sendgrid/client is never given an API key, so cancel requests are unauthenticated

Cancelled SMS reminders therefore match, and they may have a null or non-SendGrid referenceId. Sending batch_id null to SendGrid is likely to fail, and a failure aborts the whole loop (see the main finding).

response.explanation: scheduleEmailReminders.ts imports the default @sendgrid/client singleton and calls client.request() at lines 57 and 188 (POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends). The module only calls sgMail.setApiKey at line 19, and @sendgrid/mail keeps its own separate client instance, so this does not configure the @sendgrid/client singleton. No client.setApiKey appears in this file. The only other calls are in emailReminderManager.ts:26 and packages/lib/Sendgrid.ts:57. Those run inside their own functions, and nothing guarantees they ran earlier in this cron invocation.
